observations.text: SP maintained Route position at the level desired for this block, with the IP directing the initial spacing and flying part of the rejoin to Fighting Wing. Once positioned, SP held 800 ft of range at a cone of 40 degrees, inside the 500 to 1000 ft and 30 to 45 degree bands. Every repositioning, however, was initiated only after the IP called the correction. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent recognition of closure and cone drift is expected to improve.

SP assumed Route position timely on the corresponding command and, following the IP's verbal reference calls, held the aircraft no more than 200 ft forward of the line abreast position and within 50 ft of lead's height. Deviations were recognized and corrected with some delay, but no IP control input was required. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP assumed and maintained Fighting Wing position without IP prompting, working the range between 500 and 1250 ft with the cone held between 30 and 52 degrees. The two excursions outside the 30 to 45 degree band were detected and corrected in a timely manner by SP alone. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP moved to Route position promptly on command and held it accurately, remaining within 100 ft forward of the line abreast position, within 20 ft of lead's height and inside the plus 5 to minus 50 degree lateral band throughout the maneuvering. Power and bank corrections were smooth and anticipated, with no IP input at any point. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP held Route and Fighting Wing positions with negligible deviations, staying on the briefed bearing line, within 10 ft of lead's height and between 35 and 40 degrees of cone at a steady 700 to 800 ft. As leader, SP executed the maneuvers according to the handbooks with smooth movements that neither complicated nor surprised No2. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a power-lag technique that applied corrections only after the sight picture had already changed, did not maintain the Route position distance, allowing the aircraft to fall more than one half span aft of the line abreast position. The displacement developed past 60 degrees on the bearing line and the position was not regained unaided, with the result that the IP directed the corrections and flew part of the repositioning.

SP, due to a perceptual error in judging closure and lateral separation, did not maintain the Fighting Wing position according to the Techniques and Procedures Manual, letting the range open beyond 1500 ft and the cone exceed 60 degrees during lead's turn away. The briefed geometry was not restored without assistance, with the result that the IP directed the rejoin and executed part of it. Further study of the Fighting Wing rejoin geometry is required.

SP assumed Route position on the corresponding command and remained within the standards desired for this block, holding the aircraft no more than 200 ft forward of the line abreast position and within 50 ft of lead's height. Three of the four corrections, however, were initiated only after the IP's verbal reference calls and recognition of the aft drift was delayed. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier and unprompted recognition of the changing sight picture is expected to improve.

SP maintained Route position through lead's turns without any IP prompting, with the largest excursions reaching 150 ft forward of the line abreast position, 35 ft of height split and 55 degrees aft on the bearing line. All deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without IP intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP assumed the position timely on the corresponding command and held Route position accurately, staying within 100 ft forward of the line abreast position, within 20 ft of lead's height and inside the plus 5 to minus 50 degree lateral band. In Fighting Wing the range was worked between 500 and 1000 ft with the cone kept between 30 and 45 degrees. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP held Route and Fighting Wing positions with negligible deviations, with height split not exceeding 10 ft, fore and aft displacement inside 40 ft of the line abreast position and the cone stabilized near 40 degrees. Corrections were anticipated rather than reactive and the position was re-established immediately after each of lead's directional changes. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a technique that used bank alone without a matching power correction, did not maintain the Route position height, allowing the height split to exceed 50 ft and to continue diverging. The aircraft settled below the line abreast position and more than one half span aft of it, with the result that the IP terminated the maneuver and flew the repositioning.

SP, due to poor workload distribution, with lookout, radio work and position keeping attempted simultaneously, did not maintain the Fighting Wing position within the limits of the Techniques and Procedures Manual, letting the range open past 1500 ft with the cone beyond 60 degrees. Visual contact with lead was degraded and the position was not regained unaided, with the result that the IP directed the correction and executed part of the rejoin.

SP, due to late anticipation of lead's roll into the turn, did not hold the briefed bearing line in Route position, drifting to 60 degrees aft of the line abreast position and one half span behind it. The deviation was recognized and corrected only after the IP's verbal reference call, with the result of a delayed return to position that required no IP control input.

SP, due to distraction by a secondary cockpit task during the maneuvering, did not keep the Route position height within the desired band, allowing the height split to reach 50 ft above lead. The deviation was identified only after the IP's verbal prompt and the correction was applied with delay, with the result of a large power excursion before the position was restored.

SP maintained Route and Fighting Wing positions within the standards desired for this block, with the largest deviations at 150 ft forward of the line abreast position, 35 ft of height split and a cone of 52 degrees. All errors were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention. The same corrections, however, were repeated at every turn reversal rather than being anticipated. Marginal performance for the Training Section - smoother and earlier power and bank control is expected to improve.

SP assumed the position timely on the corresponding command and held Route position with accuracy and speed, keeping the aircraft inside 100 ft forward of the line abreast position and within 20 ft of lead's height without any prompting. During the transition to Fighting Wing the cone was managed between 30 and 45 degrees at ranges of 600 to 900 ft. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew Route and Fighting Wing positions with negligible deviations, holding the bearing line within a few degrees of the briefed sight picture, the height split under 10 ft and the cone stabilized between 35 and 42 degrees. As leader, SP executed the maneuvers according to the handbooks with smooth inputs that did not complicate the task for No2. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect sight picture reference taken on lead's wingtip instead of the briefed reference points, did not maintain the Route position distance and lateral placement, first closing 15 degrees ahead of the line abreast position and then falling more than one half span aft of it. The briefed position was not re-established unaided, with the result that the IP took the aircraft and repositioned the formation.

SP, due to lack of awareness of the aircraft's position relative to lead during the turn away, did not maintain the Fighting Wing cone, allowing it to exceed 60 degrees while the range opened past 1500 ft. The blind position was not called and no rejoin was initiated, with the result that the IP directed the correction and flew part of the rejoin to restore the briefed geometry.

SP, due to a delayed power reduction at the completion of the rejoin, did not stabilize the Route position within the desired distance, arriving 200 ft forward of the line abreast position and 15 degrees ahead of it on the bearing line. The overshoot was recognized and corrected only after the IP's verbal reference call, with the result that the position was re-established with delay but without IP control input.

SP, due to failure to pass the required call at the briefed point, did not assume the Fighting Wing position timely when the corresponding command was given, remaining at 1500 ft of range and 20 degrees of cone. The position was taken up only after the IP repeated the direction verbally, with the result of a delayed transition that was completed without IP control input.

SP, due to small over-corrections in bank while holding the bearing line, did not maintain the Route position height precisely, allowing the height split to reach 35 ft above lead on two occasions. Both deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention, with the result of minor excursions that did not affect the formation geometry.

SP, due to complacency on a maneuver flown repeatedly without incident, did not keep the Fighting Wing cone inside the desired band, drifting to 52 degrees at a range of 1250 ft during lead's turn. The drift was self-detected and corrected promptly, with the result of a minor deviation that required no IP intervention.

SP assumed position timely on the corresponding command and maintained Route position within the desired standards, holding the aircraft inside 100 ft forward of the line abreast position and within 20 ft of lead's height. In Fighting Wing, however, the range was worked at the upper edge of the 500 to 1000 ft band for most of the maneuvering and the cone twice touched 45 degrees. Marginal performance for the Training Section - tighter range and cone control inside the desired band is expected to improve.

SP held Route position with negligible deviations, remaining within 10 ft of lead's height and within 30 ft of the line abreast position through all of lead's turns and speed changes. Fighting Wing was flown with the cone stabilized between 35 and 42 degrees at 600 to 800 ft, with corrections anticipated rather than reactive. Above end of block MIF achieved.
